raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates right lung volume loss with mediastinal shift to the right and an absent right hilar shadow, which are classic radiographic signs of unilateral pulmonary artery agenesis (the "absent hilum" sign). While Swyer-James syndrome also presents with a small lung, it is typically associated with hyperlucency and bronchiectasis rather than the complete absence of the hilar vascular shadow seen here.
